---
title: "Numerical experiments: failures and matched diagnostic-screened accuracy"
output: html_document
params:
  manifest: null
  output: null
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
lib<-Sys.getenv("EIVGP_R_LIBRARY");if(nzchar(lib)).libPaths(c(lib,.libPaths()))
source("convergence-report.R")
report<-convergence_report(params$manifest,params$output)
```

This report is a snapshot of the selected source archives, not the final merged
manuscript dataset. It reads saved artifacts only. Optimizer nonconvergence, native
fit/prediction-stage errors, measurement diagnostic failures, and response MCMC
diagnostic failures are distinct. Missing evidence is unknown, not a pass.
A diagnostic pass is a screening result, not proof of convergence.

## Artifact readability

Unreadable artifacts remain unknown and are listed below; they are not silently
accepted or diagnosed as optimizer failures. This can also occur during a live
write, so repeat the snapshot after jobs finish.

```{r readability, echo=FALSE}
if(nrow(report$read_errors))knitr::kable(report$read_errors)else cat("All inspected saved artifacts were readable.")
```

## Failure rates

Rates use the explicitly reported assessed-stage denominators. Hard-failure rates
use resolved jobs; pending jobs are not failures. Shared measurement diagnostics
are counted as exposures for each method, not independent measurement fits.

```{r rates, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
rates<-report$failure_rates
knitr::kable(rates[,c("design","calib","method","n_planned","n_pending","n_complete","n_hard_failure","n_artifact_error","n_converged")])
for(stage in c("optimizer","measurement","response")) {
  cat("\n\n### ",stage," checks\n\n",sep="")
  cols<-c("design","calib","method",paste0(stage,c("_n_assessed","_n_failed","_n_error","_n_nonconverged","_n_unknown","_failure_rate")))
  print(knitr::kable(rates[,cols],digits=3))
}
```

## Accuracy on matched runs passing all applicable checks

Each pair uses the same replication, calibration, design, target and stratum.
Each metric uses finite scores from both methods. Positive differences mean
method A minus method B; smaller is better for RMSE, CRPS and NLPD. Coverage and
interval width require joint interpretation. MCSE measures replication variation.
Different pairs can have different matched sets. This sensitivity analysis may
select easier datasets; interpret it alongside failures and unfiltered scores.

```{r accuracy, echo=FALSE}
if(nrow(report$matched_converged_summary))knitr::kable(subset(report$matched_converged_summary,stratum=="overall"),digits=4) else cat("No matched runs have documented passes for every applicable check.")
```

The output directory contains job-level statuses, unfiltered replicate scores,
matched pairs, and the paired summary. Original-grid exports without a numerical
job registry are a separate evaluation protocol and must not be pooled into this
calibrated-comparison report.
